subject: the lavaan Note: The “Chisq” column contains standard test statistics

messages.author: 96d9ff660a5feec3
messages.subject: the lavaan Note: The “Chisq” column contains standard test statistics
parts:
Hello,


I used the anova function to compare two nested models. Model 1 is the configural model, and Model 2 is the loading model where loadings are constrained equally across groups. 

Items are a 4-point Likert-scale, so I used the WLSMV estimation. 


When I compared two models, I got the lavaan Note: The “Chisq” column contains standard test statistics, not the robust test that should be reported per model. A robust difference test is a function of two standard (not robust) statistics.


But, when the ML estimation is applied, I did not get this note. Does it mean that when the ML estimation is used, the robust test will be applied? 


Thanks! 


Ali

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: the lavaan Note: The “Chisq” column contains standard test statistics
parts: If you chose ML estimation, then there is no robust test. Robust tests are conducted with robust statistics, which are robust against the distribution assumption underlying ML estimation.

If you chose ML estimation, then there is no robust test. Robust tests are conducted with robust statistics, which are robust against the distribution assumption underlying ML estimation.
